transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Ethan Brooks (Redwood AE), Priya Kahn (Redwood SE), Liam Carter (ZenithHead of Integrations), Sofia Reyes (Zenith SA), Noah Kim (Zenith Marketplace PM)

Summary (auto): Technical integration sync for marketplace listing and reference architecture.

00:00:00 Ethan Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll go through the marketplace listing requirements and then dive into the reference architecture, Priya from the SE side will cover the deployment options and benchmarks.
00:00:22 Liam Carter: Great yeah, thanks Ethan. Quick ask from our side — we need clear network diagrams for both the VPC based integration and the private on-prem package so our infra team can eval.
00:00:35 Priya Kahn: Absolutely, we'll include both. For VPC we typically show either VPC peering with a NAT egress or direct VPC endpoints, and for Private we show the control plane connections, certs, and KMS/HSM integration points.
00:00:54 Sofia Reyes: On KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? Our compliance needs require CMKs in our tenant KMS.
00:01:05 Priya Kahn: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integration and HSM for on-prem. For hosted marketplace listings we call out the KMS support as a capability but we won't have customer keys on shared hosted. For Dedicated or Private, CMK is supported.
00:01:23 Noah Kim: For the marketplace listing, what metadata do you need? Screenshots, pricing, SLA details, integration docs?
00:01:34 Ethan Brooks: Good question. We'll need a short product description, logos, 2–3 screenshots of the console flow (onboarding, model selection, monitoring), pricing tiers (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and a reference architecture diagram. We'll share a template.
00:01:51 Priya Kahn: And include the recommended quantization/instance types by workload (low-latency chat vs high-throughput embeddings) — that helps customers pick the right SKU.
00:02:10 Liam Carter: On the reference arch detail — for VPC peering is there a recommended firewall rule set? We want to minimize open ports.
00:02:22 Priya Kahn: We recommend egress-only tunnels to Redwood control plane with port 443, strict IP allowlist from our customer-managed NAT IPs, and mTLS for control plane traffic. We'll put a sample security group and TF template in the diagram.
00:02:39 Ethan Brooks: We'll also note KV-cache and prefix caching behaviors, since customers ask about traffic patterns — sometimes transcriptions call it KV cash, lol.
00:02:52 Sofia Reyes: Haha, yeah the team saw 'KV cash' in a doc earlier and were confused.
00:03:01 Priya Kahn: On benchmarking, our standard is to run a representative workload with your devs: a mix of short chat prompts (<=128 tokens) and long prompt tests (1k tokens) and embeddings batch runs. We'll measure p95 latency, tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens.
00:03:21 Liam Carter: That sounds good. We can provision a cluster for the week of 3/30. Noah will schedule the benchmark window.
00:03:30 Noah Kim: Yep I'll schedule that. Also on marketplace — any restrictions on screenshots or branding?
00:03:38 Ethan Brooks: We prefer neutral screenshots without customer-specific PII, and logos should be SVGs when possible. We'll share guidelines.
00:03:51 Sofia Reyes: Security review — will you provide SOC 2 or ISO docs for the listing? Our procurement needs those.
00:03:59 Ethan Brooks: Yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and ISO cert references. For detailed security questionnaires we'll send the security pack and an SDQ response.
00:04:12 Priya Kahn: There's also an audit-log integration we can highlight — per-route tracing and some sample console screenshots for token-level cost breakdown.
00:04:25 Liam Carter: Nice. For private deployments we need more detail on automatic fallback policies and routing. We want the ability to route to smaller models when capacity is low, to avoid outages.
00:04:37 Priya Kahn: We support smart routing policies — latency-first or cost-first — and automatic fallback to pinned compatible model variants. We'll document canonical examples and include a YAML snippet in the ref arch.
00:04:55 Ethan Brooks: On the joint-solution packaging — we want to co-brand a reference arch doc plus a joint solution one-pager for the marketplace. Who owns the copy and who will sign off?
00:05:07 Noah Kim: Zenith can draft the first go-to-market copy and we'll review. We expect Redwood to provide technical diagrams and a few lines on capabilities.
00:05:18 Ethan Brooks: Sounds fair. We'll deliver tech diagrams; Noah draft the GTM blurb and we'll iterate.
00:05:27 Sofia Reyes: A couple technical q's — does Redwood's Dedicated offer predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools? How do autoscale policies interact with burst capacity?
00:05:39 Priya Kahn: Yes Dedicated is reserved pools with autoscale rules. Burst capacity can be configured for spikes. We'll include an example of policy configs and expected latency targets for your workloads.
00:05:56 Liam Carter: On quantization — do you have recommended profiles for FP16 vs int8? We run a lot of embeddings so cost matters.
00:06:06 Priya Kahn: We'll include quantization recommendations per model family — typically int8 for embeddings-heavy inference if fidelity checks pass, and mixed-precision for chat. Also mention quality monitoring and eval hooks to detect regressions.
00:06:23 Ethan Brooks: There's sometimes an objection about accuracy vs cost tradeoffs — we'll recommend a small eval suite you can run to check regressions post-quantization.
00:06:34 Sofia Reyes: Good. For the benchmark plan — can Redwood run a short internal run as well, to baseline, or do you prefer us to run on Zenith infra?
00:06:44 Priya Kahn: We can run a controlled baseline on Redwood Dedicated in our lab, but to validate network and infra differences we need to run on your sandbox. So both are helpful.
00:06:56 Liam Carter: Okay we'll do a two-step: Redwood baseline then Zenith infra run.
00:07:04 Noah Kim: Any legal/procurement flags we should be aware of for marketplace listing? Contract terms, data residency?
00:07:13 Ethan Brooks: Marketplace listing itself is marketing — but for enterprise deals we'll route to Dedicated/Private contracts. Data residency is handled via region selection and Private deployments. We'll share the standard marketplace T&Cs and an engagement flow.
00:07:30 Sofia Reyes: Great. Quick note — we need an example of the audit log format for our SIEM ingestion.
00:07:38 Priya Kahn: We'll attach a sample JSON audit log and a small script example for pushing to Splunk/Datadog.
00:07:49 Ethan Brooks: Great. Going to the timeline: Priya will send the listing template and sample logs this week, I'll send the ref arch draft by Monday next week, and you (Liam) will provision a sandbox and confirm the benchmark window.
00:08:04 Liam Carter: Yep that's doable.
00:08:08 --- (discussion continues, deep technical clarifications) ---
00:20:10 Priya Kahn: Deep dive — here's a sample YAML for routing policies: policy: latency_first, fallback_models: [open-7b-int8, redwood-chat-medium], batch_size_hint: dynamic. Note: transcription may mangle punctuation.
00:25:05 Sofia Reyes: For the VPC peering option, do you support private link style endpoints?
00:25:14 Priya Kahn: We have region-specific endpoint options; for Private deployments we can provide a direct private link. We'll call out differences in the ref arch doc.
00:33:40 Ethan Brooks: On observability — the console exposes token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency charts. We'll include sample screenshots and a short video clip in the listing assets.
00:40:12 Noah Kim: On joint solution — what are the measurable metrics we should promise to customers? P95 latency under X ms for chat? Cost per 1k tokens?
00:40:24 Priya Kahn: We prefer to publish recommended SLOs rather than guarantees for marketplace; for Dedicated customers we can include SLA-backed targets. We'll propose numbers in the reference doc.
00:47:01 Ethan Brooks: Okay recapping next steps and action items — Ethan share ref arch by 2026-03-22, Priya send marketplace template by 2026-03-19, Liam provision sandbox by 2026-03-24, and Noah schedule benchmark week (w/c 2026-03-30).
00:47:24 Liam Carter: Confirmed.
00:47:30 Ethan Brooks: Any other outstanding items?
00:47:33 Sofia Reyes: Security pack and SOC2 docs please.
00:47:36 Ethan Brooks: We'll attach those in the follow-up.
00:47:40 Ethan Brooks: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email with the artifacts.
00:47:45 Noah Kim: Thanks all.
00:47:47 Priya Kahn: Thanks!
00:47:52 Meeting end.
